text:
The best Kings news of the month had nothing to do with the standings. Kevin Fiala made his season debut on Nov. 13, nine months after a frightening injury at the Olympics,. The standings are harder reading: 7-11-2, 16 points, and 4-6-0 over the last 10.

Our numbers say Los Angeles has been better than that. The Kings get 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 52% at five on five, which is the profile of a playoff team. They've scored 6.9 fewer goals than their chances earned and allowed 6.6 more than expected, and our points from the play come to 22.2 against the 16 they have. That gap is the season so far.

Peter Laviolette, hired in June to open up the offense, has a top line that does it. Adrian Kempe, Artemi Panarin and Alex Laferriere have 62% of the chances and an 8-3 goal edge together. Erik Gustafsson and Brandt Clarke run the best pair at 61%.

Off the ice, Drew Doughty has hired Pat Brisson as his agent as he heads toward free agency, per Daily Faceoff, so his future will hang over the winter. The Kings are 33% to make the playoffs by our odds, low for a team playing this well and a reflection of how many points they've already left behind. What we'd watch is whether the saves come back to average, because the chances are already there.
headline: The Kings deserve better than their record
